source: California mathematics framework, Learning Commons knowledge graph, verified 2026-10-07
note: The graph shows tested standards plus their prerequisites. This roster is the whole grade, so coverage gaps are visible rather than merely absent.

5.5.OA.A.1: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.
5.5.OA.A.2: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.
5.5.OA.B.3: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules; form ordered pairs and graph them on a coordinate plane.
5.5.NBT.A.1: Recognize that a digit in one place represents 10 times what it represents to its right and 1/10 of what it represents to its left.
5.5.NBT.A.2: Explain patterns in zeros when multiplying by powers of 10, and in decimal point placement; use whole-number exponents.
5.5.NBT.A.3: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.
5.5.NBT.A.4: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.
5.5.NBT.B.5: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
5.5.NBT.B.6: Find whole-number quotients with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors.
5.5.NBT.B.7: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths.
5.5.NF.A.1: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers).
5.5.NF.A.2: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions; use benchmark fractions to assess reasonableness.
5.5.NF.B.3: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator; solve word problems with fraction or mixed-number answers.
5.5.NF.B.4: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.
5.5.NF.B.6: Solve real world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers.
5.5.NF.B.7: Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.
5.5.MD.A.1: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units, and use these conversions in multi-step problems.
5.5.MD.B.2: Make a line plot of measurements in fractions of a unit; use fraction operations on the data.
5.5.MD.C.3: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.
5.5.MD.C.4: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes.
5.5.MD.C.5: Relate volume to multiplication and addition, and solve problems involving volume.
5.5.G.A.1: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines (axes) to define a coordinate system and locate points by ordered pairs.
5.5.G.A.2: Represent real world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant, and interpret the coordinates in context.
5.5.G.B.3: Understand that attributes of a category of two-dimensional figures belong to all its subcategories.
5.5.G.B.4: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.

6.6.NS.A.1: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions; solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions.
6.6.NS.B.2: Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm.
6.6.NS.B.3: Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm.
6.6.NS.C.6.b: Understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane.
6.6.NS.C.6.c: Find and position integers and rational numbers on a number line and on a coordinate plane.
6.6.RP.A.2: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b, and use rate language.
6.6.RP.A.3: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
6.6.RP.A.3.c: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100; find the whole given a part and the percent.
6.6.EE.B.6: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving a problem.
6.6.EE.B.7: Solve problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q.
6.6.G.A.1: Find the area of triangles, special quadrilaterals and polygons by composing or decomposing.
6.6.RP.A.1: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.
6.6.RP.A.3.a: Make tables of equivalent ratios, find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane; use tables to compare ratios.
6.6.RP.A.3.b: Solve unit rate problems including those involving unit pricing and constant speed.
6.6.RP.A.3.d: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units; manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.
6.6.NS.B.4: Find the greatest common factor and least common multiple of two whole numbers; use the distributive property to express a sum with a common factor.
6.6.NS.C.5: Use positive and negative numbers to describe quantities with opposite directions or values, explaining the meaning of 0.
6.6.NS.C.6.a: Recognize opposite signs of numbers as locations on opposite sides of 0 on the number line; the opposite of the opposite is the number itself.
6.6.NS.C.7.a: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two numbers on a number line.
6.6.NS.C.7.b: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts.
6.6.NS.C.7.c: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from 0 on the number line.
6.6.NS.C.7.d: Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order.
6.6.NS.C.8: Solve problems by graphing points in all four quadrants; use coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points.
6.6.EE.A.1: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.
6.6.EE.A.2.a: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers.
6.6.EE.A.2.b: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms (sum, term, product, factor, quotient, coefficient).
6.6.EE.A.2.c: Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables, including formulas, using the order of operations.
6.6.EE.A.3: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.
6.6.EE.A.4: Identify when two expressions are equivalent.
6.6.EE.B.5: Understand solving an equation or inequality as finding which values make it true; use substitution to check.
6.6.EE.B.8: Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c for a real-world or mathematical condition; represent solutions on a number line.
6.6.EE.C.9: Use variables for two quantities that change together; write an equation for the dependent variable and relate it to graphs and tables.
6.6.G.A.2: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths; apply V = l w h and V = b h.
6.6.G.A.3: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices; find side lengths from coordinates.
6.6.G.A.4: Represent three-dimensional figures using nets made up of rectangles and triangles, and use the nets to find surface area.
6.6.SP.A.1: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data.
6.6.SP.A.2: Understand that a data set has a distribution described by its center, spread, and overall shape.
6.6.SP.A.3: Recognize that a measure of center summarizes a data set with one number, while a measure of variation describes how its values vary.
6.6.SP.B.4: Display numerical data in plots on a number line, including dot plots, histograms, and box plots.
6.6.SP.B.5: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context.

7.7.RP.A.2: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.
7.7.RP.A.3: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems.
7.7.NS.A.1.d: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.
7.7.NS.A.2.c: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.
7.7.NS.A.2.d: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division.
7.7.NS.A.3: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers.
7.7.EE.B.4: Use variables to represent quantities and construct simple equations and inequalities.
7.7.SP.B.3: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions.

grades_note: Grades 5 and 6 are the complete roster (grade 6 completed 2026-10-12 from the Learning Commons knowledge graph). Grade 7 holds only the standards reachable from grade 5 through the Coherence Map, or already tested.
